text: Gratiam et pacem a Deo Patre nostro, et Domino Jesu Christo.
note: *Grātiam* capital: the greeting opens its own sentence after the address of 1:1, word for word as your settled 1 Cor 1:3 (*Grātiam et pācem ā Deō Patre nostrō, et Dominō Jēsū Chrīstō.*) and 2 Cor 1:2; *Patre* capital, God the Father (decision 20; *nostrō* lower case); no paragraph, as 1 Cor 1:3 and 2 Cor 1:2 (the BSB's break here not taken) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Nam vos omnes (testis mihi Deus est) digna Jesu Christo adfectione desidero:
note: a space before the parenthesis (the draft's *omnes(testis*; 1573 *omnes ( teſtis*, canvas 898); the words and marks otherwise as the draft (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Et nonnulli quidem invide, ac dissentientes, nonnulli etiam quod ita sentiant, Christum praedicant.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 1:14 ends a sentence and Paul turns from his chains to the preachers and their motives (1:15–18), a new step (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quamobrem, si quae est in Christo confirmatio, si quod caritatis solatium, si qua Spiritus communio, si qua commiseratio ac misericordia,
note: *Spīritūs* capital: "any sharing in the Spirit" (NRSV; BSB "fellowship with the Spirit", KJV "of the Spirit"; κοινωνία πνεύματος), the Holy Spirit (decision 20), as your settled Rom 15:30 *Spīritūs cāritātem*, 2 Cor 13:14 *Sānctī Spīritūs commūniō* (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: qui cum in Dei forma foret, \\q2 non rapinae habuit suam cum Deo aequalitatem,
note: the hymn of 2:6–11 as poetry, as the BSB sets it (its 2:6 *b q1*); Paul's own words, not a quotation, so no \\qt and no marks, as your settled Rom 11:33–36 (the doxology set as the BSB's poetry, *b q1*); two lines, Castellio's two clauses for the BSB's three; *quī* lower case, the sentence running on from 2:5 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: sed se ipsum eo usque ad nihilum redegit, \\q2 ut, sumpta servili forma, \\q2 factus sit hominum similis: \\q1 et figura repertus ut homo,
note: poetry continued, lines after the BSB (*emptied Himself / taking the form of a servant / being made in human likeness*); *et figūrā repertus ut homō* is the BSB's first line of 2:8, here in 2:7 as in 1573 and the KJV's numbering, a new q1; *homō,* with a comma for the draft's full stop, as 1573 (*vt homo,* then *ſeſe adeò deiecit*, canvas 899, page image): the participle *repertus* goes with *dējēcit* (σχήματι εὑρεθεὶς ὡς ἄνθρωπος, ἐταπείνωσεν ἑαυτόν) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: sese adeo dejecit, \\q1 ut obediens fuerit usque ad mortem, \\q2 et quidem mortem crucis.
note: poetry continued, lines after the BSB (*He humbled Himself / and became obedient to death— / even death on a cross*); *sēsē* lower case, continuing 2:7's sentence, as 1573's *ſeſe* (canvas 899) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quapropter Deus eum summopere extulit, \\q2 et nomine donavit omnium nominum summo,
note: the hymn's second stanza, with the BSB's stanza break (*b q1*), two lines after the BSB (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: ut ad Jesu nomen omne se genu flectat, \\q2 caelestium, et terrestrium, et subterraneorum:
note: poetry continued, two lines after the BSB; *omne sē genū flectat* echoes Isa 45:23, woven into the *ut* clause with no formula: an allusion, unmarked (the BSB has no quotation marks; your settled Rom 14:11 quotes the verse after *scrīptum est* in \\qt) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Omnisque lingua confiteatur, Dominum esse Jesum Christum, \\q2 ad Dei Patris gloriam.
note: the hymn's last two lines, as the BSB; *Patris* capital, God the Father (decision 20; NRSV "to the glory of God the Father"); *Omnisque* keeps its capital after 2:10's colon, as your settled books do after a colon (1 Cor 41 : 1, Rom 54 : 1); 2:12's paragraph (the draft's) closes the poetry (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Necessarium autem putavi, Epaphroditum, fratrem et collegam, commilitonemque meum, vestrum autem apostolum, et mei muneris vicarium, ad vos mittere.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 2:24 ends a sentence and Paul turns from Timothy to Epaphroditus (2:25–30), a new step (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Videte canes, videte malos operarios, videte concisos.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): after 3:1's full stop Paul turns abruptly to the warning against the circumcisers (*Vidēte canēs*, 3:2–11), a new step (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Nos enim sumus circumcisi, qui Spiritu Deum colimus, et in Christo Jesu gloriamur, non carne freti:
note: *Spīritū* capital: the circumcision that worships "in the Spirit of God" (NRSV; BSB "by the Spirit of God"), set against *carne*, as your settled Rom 2:29 *quæ cordis est, Spīritū, nōn litterīs* (decision 20). The less certain way: the TR's πνεύματι Θεῷ λατρεύοντες, which Castellio translates (*spīritū Deum colimus*), is "worship God in the spirit" (KJV lower case), as your settled John 4:23–24 *in spīritū et vēritāte colent* lower case (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Sed quae mihi lucra erant, ea propter Christum pro damno habui.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 3:6 ends the list of Paul's credentials with a full stop and *Sed* turns to their loss for Christ (3:7–11), a new step (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quinimmo omnia damnum esse puto, propter cognitionis Christi Jesu, Domini mei, praestantiam, propter quam omnium jacturam feci, eaque pro stercoribus habeo, ut Christum lucrer,
note: *lucrer,* with a comma for the draft's full stop, as 1573 (*vt Chriſtum lucrer ,* then *& mihi in eo ſuppetat*, canvas 900, page image): 3:9's *et mihi in eō suppetat* is the second purpose clause after *ut* (ἵνα Χριστὸν κερδήσω, καὶ εὑρεθῶ ἐν αὐτῷ), and the draft's full stop left it without a verb to hang on (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: et mihi in eo suppetat, nec habeam justitiam meam, quae a lege pendeat, sed in fide Christo habenda positam, pendentem a Deo justitiam in fide sitam,
note: *et* lower case, the sentence running on from 3:8 (above); *sitam,* with a comma for the draft's full stop, as 1573 (*in fide ſitam,* then *eum*, canvas 900, page image): 3:10's gerund *cognōscendō* continues the same sentence (τοῦ γνῶναι αὐτόν) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: eum, ejusque et resurrectionis vim, et suppliciorum communitatem cognoscendo, dum ad ejus mortem conformor:
note: *eum* lower case, continuing 3:9 (1573 *eum*, canvas 900); the BSB's break here not taken, as the sentence runs on (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Si qua ad mortuorum resurrectionem perveniam.
note: a full stop for the draft's comma (1573 has the comma, *perueniam,* canvas 900): the long sentence of 3:8–11 ends here, as in the Greek (νεκρῶν.) and the BSB and KJV, and 3:12 opens a sentence of its own (*Nōn quia … sed persequor*), with the draft's paragraph there; otherwise the paragraph would begin in mid-sentence with *nōn*. *Sī* keeps its capital after 3:10's colon (settled practice) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Non quia jam consecutus sim, aut jam perfectus, sed persequor, ut comprehendam, quatenus a Christo Jesu sum comprehensus.
note: *Nōn* capital, opening the sentence after 3:11's full stop (above), with the draft's paragraph (the BSB's) kept (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quorum exitus est exitium: qui et ventrem pro deo habent, et gloriam sibi in sua turpitudine collocant: qui terrestria sapiunt.
note: *deō* lower case: they hold their belly for a god (NRSV and BSB "their god is the belly", ὧν ὁ θεὸς ἡ κοιλία), not God (decision 20), as your settled 2 Cor 4:4 *hujus sæculī deus* and Exod 7:1 *Pharaōnī deum efficiō*; 1573 prints *Deo* (canvas 900), as it capitalizes every *Deus* (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Nam nostra quidem obversatio in caelis est, unde etiam Servatorem manemus Dominum Jesum Christum,
note: *Servātōrem* capital: the Saviour, Christ (decision 20 names *Servātor*; σωτῆρα), as your settled *Servātōrem* (3 : 1 lower case) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Gaudete in Domino semper; iterum dicam, gaudete.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): after the appeal to Euodia and Syntyche (4:2–3) Paul turns to the whole church (*Gaudēte in Dominō semper*, 4:4–7), a new step; the semicolon as the draft (1573 a colon) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Ceterum, fratres, quae vera sint, quae gravia, quae justa, quae casta, quae amabilia, quae fausta, si qua virtus, et si qua laus est, ea cogitate,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 4:7 ends with a full stop and *Cēterum, frātrēs* opens the closing exhortation (4:8–9), as *Cēterum, meī frātrēs* at 3:1 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Deo autem Patrique nostro gloria in perpetua saecula: Amen.
note: *Patrīque* capital, God the Father (decision 20; NRSV "to our God and Father"; *nostrō* lower case), as 1:2 and 2:11; the colon before *Āmēn* as 1573 (canvas 900) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Domini nostri Jesu Christi gratia adsit vobis omnibus: Amen. \\cls Missa Roma per Epaphroditum.
note: the subscription set apart as \\cls after the verse (decision 37), as 1573 sets it in italics under the blessing (*Miſsa Roma per Epaphroditum.*, canvas 900, page image) and as Rom 16:27, 1 Cor 16:24, 2 Cor 13:14; a full stop after it, as 1573; *omnibus: Āmēn.* with 1573's colon (page image), as 4:20 (Claude, 2026-11-11)
